title: Five(ish) Minute Dance Lesson: Merengue, Level 1

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Ricardo and Elba teach with clear step-by-step breakdowns, combining historical context with detailed biomechanical instructions. They use visual aids, partner demonstrations, and positive reinforcement to guide students through basic Merengue steps and turns.

lesson_structure.note: Instructors introduce themselves and the dance
Origin of Merengue and musical instruments
Partner dancing with knee bends and traveling
Full group dancing with live band

cues: bend one knee at the time
keep your feet flat on the floor
common_mistakes: hitting each other's legs when bending knees
letting hand go during turns (spaghetti arms)
safety: keep elbows down to prevent accidents from happening

steps_taught.name: Basic Merengue Steps
steps_taught.description: Stepping and dragging feet while bending alternating knees

steps_taught.name: Basic Turn
steps_taught.description: Clockwise turn with loose hand grip and elbow down

what_hinders: some transitions between solo and partner work are fast

quotes.text: You're going to pretend that you're tired.
You're going to drag your feet instead of taking steps.
So that when the knees are bending you're actually not hitting each other.

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor demonstrates posture with hands on waist and slight knee bending

extraction.distinctive_method: Using illustrated graphic overlays that appear on screen to emphasize key body positions, knee bends, and footwork while the instructor speaks.
